input.reasoning_summary:
All three challenges have been refuted by the evidence:

H1 (Did gross margin percentage increase or remain flat?): REFUTED. Multiple passages from the Q2 FY2026 10-Q (E13, E18) explicitly confirm that gross margin percentage decreased in the quarter ended December 31, 2025. The numeric check also confirms the decline from 68.69% to 68.04%.

H2 (Was the decline primarily driven by other factors?): REFUTED. While E15 shows that the More Personal Computing segment had gross margin percentage increases due to sales mix, the overall company-level statements (E13, E18) explicitly attribute the company-wide gross margin percentage decrease to "continued investments in AI infrastructure" as the primary driver. The filing states AI infrastructure was the driver "offset in part by" other factors, indicating AI infrastructure was the net cause.

H3 (Did efficiency gains offset AI infrastructure costs?): REFUTED. E18 and E13 both state that efficiency gains "offset in part" the AI infrastructure costs, but the net result was still a decrease in gross margin percentage. The word "offset in part" indicates partial mitigation, not full offset. AI infrastructure costs remained the net cause of the decline.

The initial verdict of SUPPORTED remains correct. The evidence consistently shows that: (1) gross margin percentage declined in Q2 FY2026 ended December 31, 2025, and (2) this decline was driven by AI infrastructure costs, with the filing explicitly stating this causal relationship multiple times.
